For middle school we just had our 8th Grade produce a chess set. We focused on working within a set outer dimension and focusing on Alignment, symmetry and composite shapes. Mirror's Edge: Catalyst

According to this article, they're taking out gun combat because they think it will be a statement. They're not wrong, but they're making the wrong statement. By taking guns out, they've eliminated to much puzzle potential and speedrunning tactics which is huge in Mirror's Edge. With guns you can take out a guard, grab his weapon, do some climbing, shoot a window, and jump through the gap so you don't lose momentum breaking the glass. With guns you realize that you are fighting armoured guards with multiple magazines in their pockets where you only have ~12 rounds. With guns there is a sense of helplessness when you're under fire and you have around 3 rounds left, or maybe you don't even know how many you have because there isn't a HUD. With guns you realize that using weapons for everything is a unoptimal as fuck in a game where you can run on walls and combo enemies to death efficiently.

Removing guns in Mirror's Edge is like removing the orange portal in Portal. It will just make the game seem illogical and linear as opposed to open and free. Without guns you're going to have many moments where you take out a guard and their friend will just chill around the corner and shoot as soon as you turn and the only thing you can do is run and hope for the best. They claim that removing guns from the game is beneficial and will "promote creativity" but its either going to end up being "charge at everyone you see and pray you don't get shot" or "charge at everyone and don't worry about getting shot because you have 'flow'".

I'm almost certain this game is going to absolutely suck because the devs are now limited in the difficulty they can make enemies and the number of enemies they can spawn at a time because there isn't the option of simply fighting then off and picking up a gun when things get hairy.

I'm gonna sound like every fanboy out there, but the first Mirror's Edge had it right.
